'''Jenő Hunyady''' (28 April 1838 in [[Pest, Hungary|Pest]] &ndash; 26 December 1889 in [[Budapest]]) was a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]] [[mathematician]] noted for his work on [[conic section]]s and [[linear algebra]], specifically on [[determinants]]. He received his Ph.D. in [[University of Göttingen|Göttingen]] (1864). He worked at the [[Budapest University of Technology and Economics|University of Technology]] of Budapest. He was elected a corresponding member (1867), member (1883) of the [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]]. From 1885 he actively participated in the informal meetings of what became later the [[János Bolyai Mathematical Society|Mathematical and Physical Society]] of Hungary.
